name: tinysparql
desc: Low-footprint RDF triple store with SPARQL 1.1 interface
why: A small RDF triple store with SPARQL, a rare chance to query a semantic graph database locally.

brief.what_it_is: TinySPARQL is a low-footprint RDF triple store library with a SPARQL 1.1 interface, written as a C library built on GObject and Gio. Per the homepage, it exposes a TrackerSparqlConnection for holding a connection to a triple store, prepared statements, cursors for iterating query results, and a Notifier for change events. The homepage's API reference lists a tinysparql command-line executable in the Homebrew metadata, but I did not see its usage documented in what I fetched. The project is a fork-lineage successor to Tracker, and its homepage calls it Tsparql 3.0.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes it simply as a low-footprint RDF triple store with a SPARQL 1.1 interface. The README gives no further problem statement beyond the one-line project description.
brief.how_it_works: Applications open a TrackerSparqlConnection to a store and run SPARQL queries and updates through it; results come back through TrackerSparqlCursor and statements can be prepared as TrackerSparqlStatement. TrackerEndpoint, TrackerEndpointDBus and TrackerEndpointHttp can make a store available to other processes over D-Bus or to other hosts over HTTP. Batch, Resource and NamespaceManager help assemble transactions, in-memory RDF resources and prefix mappings.
brief.install_notes: Homepage build info: C header tinysparql.h and pkg-config file tinysparql-3.0. Listed dependencies are GObject 2.0 and Gio 2.0. Beyond the Homebrew package, I saw no first-run or configuration steps, and no install commands in the README, which is essentially empty.
brief.standout: It is a small RDF triple store you can query with SPARQL 1.1 entirely locally, from a C library with GObject bindings, which is unusual next to heavier semantic graph databases. The ontology set (Nepomuk, NIE, NFO, NCO and others) ships with it and is listed in the docs.
brief.status: Active on the homepage: it advertises version 3.12.0 and includes a 'Migrating from 2.x to 3.0' guide and a per-class API reference. The GitLab project page shows creation on May 23, 2018, but no last release date or last commit date was visible, so recent activity is not confirmed.
brief.caveats: The GitLab README is a single line reading 'GNU LGPLv2.1', so the project documentation lives on the homepage. The license is inconsistent between sources: the homepage says GPL-2.1-or-later while GitLab says GNU LGPLv2.1, and this should be checked before reuse. The homepage refers to a 'Commandline reference' and a 'Sandboxing and portals' page, which I did not fetch. The brew description calls it a 'triple store' but the project itself is a library, so expect to use its API rather than a standalone database server.
quotes: Low-footprint RDF triple store with SPARQL 1.1 interface
TrackerSparqlConnection holds a connection to a RDF triple store.
TrackerNotifier allows receiving notification on changes in the data stored by a TrackerSparqlConnection.

judge.reason: A compact local RDF store makes SPARQL and semantic-graph querying accessible from ordinary applications, opening a useful, unfamiliar data model beyond generic database plumbing.

entry.title: TinySPARQL
entry.tldr: A small RDF triple store you query with SPARQL 1.1, built as a GObject C library and the successor to GNOME's Tracker.
entry.deeper_look:
TinySPARQL is a C library that holds RDF data and answers SPARQL 1.1 queries. Its homepage describes it as a "Low-footprint RDF triple store with SPARQL 1.1 interface". An application opens a TrackerSparqlConnection to a store, runs queries and updates through it, and reads results back through a cursor. Statements can be prepared, and a Notifier reports changes to the stored data.

The homepage describes it as the successor to Tracker (version 3.x), and it ships with a set of ontologies (Nepomuk, NIE, NFO, NCO and others) listed in the docs. The brief gives no stated motivation beyond the one-line description, so the why is best read off the API: a store that lives inside a program rather than in a separate database server.

The idea underneath is the triple: everything is a subject, a predicate and an object, and a query is a pattern matched against a graph. SPARQL is the standard language for those patterns. Stores can also be exposed to other processes over D-Bus, or to other hosts over HTTP, through the endpoint classes.

The brew formula installs a `tinysparql` executable. The brief did not capture its usage, so start with its help output. The homepage mentions a command-line reference page that was not fetched.

try_this.what_happens: Lists the subcommands the command-line tool offers, which is the way into the rest of it.

entry.whats_unique: It is a small, local SPARQL 1.1 store embedded as a GObject library, with a standard ontology set included, rather than a heavyweight graph database server.
entry.caveats: It is mainly a library, so expect to use its C API (or GObject bindings) rather than a standalone database; the README is one line, docs live on the homepage, and sources disagree on the license wording.
